summary: Hungry Creek Peak lookout (Klamath NF): 1937 cabin on a 10-ft tower, removed before 1986; a foundation remains. Built year conflicts (1937 vs 1938).

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10 foot timber tower
facts.status_note: Structure removed before 1986; a foundation remains at the site per the register
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

access.note: On Klamath National Forest land per the register; no route, closure or current access is described in the sources read

events.note: A 1932 diary entry refers to the old Hungry Creek lookout, so a lookout predates the current one
During a heavy lightning storm, a CCC enrollee from Hilt was sent up as emergency lookout (July 7, 1934 diary)
Register date for the present cabin on a 10 foot timber tower; the site title was accepted February 13, 1937
Forest Lookouts history says the new lookout was constructed by CCC Camp F176 in 1938 (register says 1937)
Clara Williams, widow of Ranger John Williams, went to work as lookout on June 1, 1954 and served 17 years
Registered April 16, 2020 as FFLOS US 2024, CA 141; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: The register describes a cabin on a 10 foot timber tower (about 3.0 m); no source read gives 4.3 m

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the lookout was built in 1937. The Forest Lookouts history says the land title was accepted in February 1937 and the new lookout was constructed by a CCC camp in 1938. The story reports both and says the accounts disagree.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. Brief height 4.3 m conflicts with the register's 10 foot tower; correction proposed. Built year conflicts (1937 register vs 1938 CCC construction in the Forest Lookouts history). Removal is only bounded (before 1986), so no removal event. Access 'public' is inferred from national forest land. The 2009 'Foundation remains' photo is cited by caption only; no image URL was captured, so no photo entry.
